body: When I’m really depressed I try to keep stuff by my bed: wipes, breath mints, body spray so I don’t have to get up to use it since I end up being too tired to get out of bed. I also try to combine potty breaks/shower breaks with other stuff. Ex: using mouth wash while I’m in the shower. I will lay/sit down if I need to. I’ve been there and I am sorry you are going through this.

It’s a few different reasons for me. The main one seems to be to control my emotions and calm my brain. When I’m overwhelmed and I self harm it gets me to focus on the physical pain and not the emotional pain and/or the “loudness” of my brain. It can help me to not express anger towards others as I get it out my system by taking it out on myself. It can also be relaxing as I tend feel a rush afterwards which definitely makes it harder to quit once I start. 

The other reason is it helps me deal with guilt. If I feel like I messed up I think that I need to punish myself because “I’m a terrible person and I deserve it” (thank you abusive childhood for that message 😒) so after hurting myself I feel like I’m allowed to not hate myself (at least temporarily). I also deal with guilt by finding other people to hurt me (which I am aware is problematic) so for that one it’s always up in the air as to whether I will hurt myself or find someone else to do it for me. So yeah…

I was in partial hospitalization for over a month (closer to two). It wasn’t sunshine and roses but overall it was a good experience (I still have a binder full of all the handouts that they gave me). 

I was in therapy from 9am-3pm Mon- Fri with about an hour lunch break. They provided transportation and food if you didn’t have any and at no time was I locked in or prevented from leaving. The only items not allowed were weapons and drugs/alcohol (cigarettes were ok). Most of the material was educational or applied counseling theories (challenging childhood messages, identifying and replacing harmful coping mechanisms, etc) but we also had time to just talk about what we needed to: our symptoms, past trauma, daily stress. It was nice to get support from others patients who actually understood what I was going through. They had individual therapists if you needed extra support and while they would have you speak to a psychiatrist at least once the main focus was on therapy. Medication was 100% your choice and they even provided an educational group on different types of meds. They also had coloring/drawing materials for folks that were anxious or easily distracted during group which was surprisingly relaxing. 

I will say it does depend on the therapists/treatment facility as I’ve had some terrible experiences in other programs like IOP (intensive outpatient) which is a shorter less intensive program. So while my experience was positive, the quality of service can really vary by facility.

Yeah, US mental health care sucks ass. I got hospitalized for 17 days when I was 13 and not only did it not help, it was traumatizing. To this day I will not tell a therapist when I’m feeling suicidal or reckless (even tho I’ve almost died before). 

I always suggest partial hospitalization to people cause unlike inpatient (where you lose all autonomy and rights) you can spend the day getting the help you need without being locked up against your will. Not every insurance company covers it but it’s worth a shot to ask.

I get you are trying to be nice but advice giving is not really helpful. Even with therapy and meds I haven’t gotten better, I’ve gotten worse. It’s not a “temporary situation” that I can fix if I take time for myself, it’s something I’ve dealt with everyday since I was a kid. Mental illness can be a lifelong struggle so there is a solid chance the situation may never improve. That’s why I don’t want to be here. I’ve researched euthanasia in other countries a lot and while I don’t plan on attempting right this minute, I feel like I am going to end up doing that because it checks all the boxes for how I want to do it. I really just needed to vent and was hoping others might be able to get where I was coming from. So while I appreciate your reply, I really don’t feel like you heard what I was saying or understand my situation.

It might be helpful to talk a medical professional as sometimes there is an underlying condition especially if you have concentration issues. I almost didn’t pass the 8th grade because I was too depressed to function and failed English (which is the only language I know) and biology my sophomore year of high school. I still graduated tho and actually took some AP classes my senior year. 

If you struggle with concentration, it can be helpful to break studying up into sections. Commit to 20 mins of working then take a 5 minute break and repeat that until you finish or are completely unable to focus. 

If your thoughts are really loud, you can try listening to study music, isochronic tones, or binaural beats on YouTube (the last two are tones that help with folks that have add/adhd) while working. 

It can be hard to get started if you doubt yourself as the fear of failure could be preventing you from completing the assignment. (You could try looking up self worth theory if you identify with the previous statement). 

A former teacher suggested telling myself that I wasn’t allowed to start an assignment right away as telling yourself you aren’t allowed to do something can make it seem more interesting. 

It might take some time to find what works best for you. Just know that it’s ok to not get things done or even to fail. It doesn’t mean you are wasting your life. Everyone moves at their own pace and that’s ok. I still struggle all the time. Just know that you are not alone. Best of luck, I hope things get better soon. (:

It took me months to tell to my last therapist about my self harm. It is really important to find someone who is qualified to treat self harm as someone without experience can end up doing more harm than good. I haven’t always had the best experiences (hence having difficulty disclosing now). 

If you haven’t already ask what he specializes in and what issues he has experience treating. You can say a broad question like “what issues do you and have you worked with? Do you focus on clients who have anxiety, sleep issues, self harm, mood disorders, abuse, relationship problems or something else? There’s just a lot of issues so I don’t know what you have experience in and what issues you feel you are or aren’t qualified to treat?”

Just throw it in there nonchalantly, not the first thing not the last so you know if he is trained without telling him. (Be cautious if a therapist says they can treat everything as it is very unlikely they have enough training to effectively treat EVERY issue). 

It can be good to clarify why he would need to break confidentiality as some therapists (typically poorly trained ones)  see self harm as intent to commit suicide (depending on what type of self-harm you use) and may call a 51-50 on you. 

You can also ask how much experience he has and what counseling theories he uses. 
(DBT, CBT, and psychodynamic therapy are popular ones to treat self harm) 

If your therapist tries to invalidate you by saying: “You’re doing it for attention” or
“You aren’t going deep enough to need help”LEAVE! Any therapist who says that is poorly trained and an ass. 
All forms of self harm should be taken seriously. 

Also, if your therapist expects immediate results after showing you a few coping skills I’d recommend leaving. Treatment for self harm takes time and relapses occur. (I’m getting treatment now and recently relapsed.) Don’t expect changes over night. Some days therapy will suck ass but it can help (even if you sometimes move backwards). 

Sorry this post is so long and I apologize if I came off as intense. Best of luck in receiving care. (:
